CapabilityCategory.description:
The only categories v0.1 compiles (specification 3.1).

Three, not five. Paging is not its own category — specification 3.1 puts
pagination and opening a detail link both under ``navigate`` — and reading is
not a capability at all, it is what a snapshot already provides. Accepting
names the specification does not define would let a compiler invent a category
that no downstream risk rule or MCP client knows how to treat.
CapabilityCategory.title: CapabilityCategory

CapabilityTemplate.description:
A reusable, portable, non-executable capability (specification 7.8).

Two invariants are enforced here rather than left to the compiler, because a
template violating either would be persisted, exported, and only fail much
later at binding time:

Every step's ``target_ref`` has a locator chain. A plan referring to a target
the template cannot locate is a plan that cannot run, and discovering that at
execution time would mean a partially performed sequence.

Every locator chain is referred to by a step. An unused chain is either a
compiler mistake or a step that went missing, and both are worth failing on
while the template is still being built.
CapabilityTemplate.title: CapabilityTemplate

Confidence.description: Specification 7.4. Only ``medium`` and ``high`` may become templates.
Confidence.title: Confidence

Evidence.description:
One recorded observation supporting a claim.

``element_id`` and ``collection_id`` are snapshot-scoped: they name something
in the snapshot this IR was built from, not something in the live page. A
reader that wants the live element must re-resolve it, which is exactly the
boundary specification 7.7 draws.
Evidence.title: Evidence

ExpectedEffect.description: What must be observed for an execution to count as success (11.3).
ExpectedEffect.title: ExpectedEffect

IRWarning.description:
Something the reading could not do, reported rather than swallowed.

``code`` is stable and machine-readable; ``message`` is for a person. An agent
branching on prose would break the first time the wording improved.
IRWarning.title: IRWarning

LocatorCandidate.description:
One way to find an element again.

``key`` holds the matching value for the candidate kind: the ``id`` value, the
control ``name``, the accessible name, the label text, or a structural path
rooted at the nearest landmark or form ancestor. A structural path may carry
tag-index information, but execution must never fall back to a global
nth-child-only path, a bounding box, a screenshot coordinate, or a selector
supplied by an external agent.
LocatorCandidate.title: LocatorCandidate

LocatorChain.description:
All applicable candidates for one element, plus the primary candidate.

Re-resolution (specification 7.7) walks ``candidates`` in priority order and
accepts only an exactly-one match. Zero matches and ambiguous matches both
continue to the next candidate; the closest element is never chosen.
LocatorChain.title: LocatorChain

LocatorKind.description:
Candidate kinds in priority order (specification 7.6).

Lower value means higher priority, so a chain sorts by ``kind`` directly.
LocatorKind.title: LocatorKind

PlanStep.description:
One step of an execution plan, written against a target name.

``target_ref`` is a name inside the template, never an element ID. Element IDs
belong to one snapshot of one session; a template outlives both.
PlanStep.title: PlanStep

RejectedCandidate.description:
Something compilable-looking that was deliberately not compiled.

``risk`` is present whenever it could be classified, and classifying the risk
of something being refused is not wasted work: an agent told only that a form
was skipped will try to reach it another way, while one told the form is a
high-risk POST has been given the reason.
RejectedCandidate.title: RejectedCandidate

Risk.description:
Why a capability is or is not safe to run (specification 10.1).

Classified by side effect rather than by mechanism: the same click is harmless
on a search form and irreversible on a delete button, so the button is not
what decides.
Risk.title: Risk

RiskLevel.description:
Specification 10.1. Only ``LOW`` is ever executable.

``CRITICAL`` exists even though nothing may run at that level, and the reason
is that a level nobody can name cannot be reported. An agent asking what a page
offers deserves to be told that the delete button was seen and refused, rather
than to find it silently absent.
RiskLevel.title: RiskLevel

SideEffect.description:
What running a capability does to the world (specification 10.1).

The five values are the specification's, and the ordering between them is the
whole risk model: risk is decided by consequence, never by mechanism. The same
click is ``NONE`` on a search form and ``DESTRUCTIVE_OR_FINANCIAL`` on a
"close account" button, so the click tells you nothing.
SideEffect.title: SideEffect

description:
Everything one snapshot compiled to.

Carries ``snapshot_id`` because every claim in it is about one observation.
Two reports of the same page class are comparable only through their
templates' page signatures, never by equality.
title: CompilationReport
